questions.q: What were the chief priests and scribes considering how to do?
questions.a: They were considering how to stealthily arrest Jesus and then kill him.

questions.q: Why did the chief priests and scribes not want to act during the Feast of Unleavened Bread?
questions.a: They were worried that a riot would arise among the people.

questions.q: What did a woman do to Jesus at the house of Simon the leper?
questions.a: A woman broke a vial of costly liquid and poured it on Jesus’ head.

questions.q: For what were some rebuking the woman?
questions.a: Some were rebuking the woman for not selling the perfume and giving the money to the poor.

questions.q: What did Jesus say the woman had done for him?
questions.a: Jesus said the woman had anointed his body for burial.

questions.q: What promise did Jesus make about what the woman had done?
questions.a: Jesus promised that wherever the gospel was preached in the whole world, what the woman had done would be spoken of in memory of her.

questions.q: Why did Judas Iscariot go away to the chief priests?
questions.a: Judas Iscariot went away to the chief priests so that he might deliver Jesus to them.

questions.q: How did the disciples find the place where they would all eat the Passover?
questions.a: Jesus told them to go into the city and follow a man carrying a pitcher of water, and then ask him where the guest room was that they would use to eat the Passover.

questions.q: What did Jesus say as they were reclining at the table and eating?
questions.a: Jesus said that one of the disciples eating with him would betray him.

questions.q: Which disciple did Jesus say would betray him?
questions.a: Jesus said that the disciple dipping bread with him in the bowl would betray him.

questions.q: What did Jesus say about the destiny of the disciple who betrayed him?
questions.a: Jesus said that it would have been better for him if he had not been born.

questions.q: What did Jesus say as he gave the disciples the broken bread?
questions.a: Jesus said, “Take this. This is my body.”

questions.q: What did Jesus say as he gave the disciples the cup?
questions.a: Jesus said, “This is my blood of the covenant, the blood that is poured out for many.”

questions.q: When did Jesus say he would again drink of this fruit of the vine?
questions.a: Jesus said he would again drink of this fruit of the vine on the day when he drank it anew in the kingdom of God.

questions.q: At the Mount of Olives, what did Jesus predict about his disciples?
questions.a: Jesus predicted that his disciples would all fall away because of him.

questions.q: What did Jesus tell Peter after Peter said he would never fall away?
questions.a: Jesus told Peter that before the rooster crowed twice, Peter would deny Jesus three times.

questions.q: What did Jesus tell his three disciples to do while he prayed?
questions.a: Jesus told them to remain there and watch.

questions.q: For what did Jesus pray?
questions.a: Jesus prayed that this hour might pass from him.

questions.q: What was Jesus willing to accept as an answer to his prayer to the Father?
questions.a: Jesus was willing to accept whatever the Father’s will was for him.

questions.q: What did Jesus find when he returned to the three disciples?
questions.a: Jesus found the three disciples sleeping.

questions.q: What did Jesus find the second time he returned from praying?
questions.a: Jesus found the three disciples sleeping.

questions.q: What did Jesus find the third time he returned from praying?
questions.a: Jesus found the three disciples sleeping.

questions.q: What sign did Judas give to show the guards which person was Jesus?
questions.a: Judas kissed Jesus to show which person was Jesus.

questions.q: What did Jesus say was being done in his arrest to fulfill scripture?
questions.a: Jesus said that scripture was being fulfilled because they came to arrest him like a robber, with swords and clubs.

questions.q: What did those with Jesus do when Jesus was arrested?
questions.a: Those with Jesus left him and fled.

questions.q: What did a young man who was following Jesus do when Jesus was arrested?
questions.a: The young man left his linen garment there and ran away naked.

questions.q: Where was Peter as Jesus was taken to the high priest?
questions.a: Peter sat among the guards, near a fire to keep warm.

questions.q: What was wrong with the testimony against Jesus given to the Council?
questions.a: The testimony against Jesus was false and did not agree.

questions.q: What question did the high priest ask Jesus about who Jesus was?
questions.a: The high priest asked Jesus if he was the Christ, the son of the Blessed.

questions.q: What was Jesus’ answer to the high priest’s question?
questions.a: Jesus answered by saying, “I am.”

questions.q: Hearing Jesus’ answer, of what did the high priest say Jesus was guilty?
questions.a: The high priest said that Jesus was guilty of blasphemy.

questions.q: What did they do to Jesus after condemning him as one who deserved death?
questions.a: They spit on him, struck him, and beat him.

questions.q: What was Peter’s answer to the servant girl who said that Peter was with Jesus?
questions.a: Peter answered that he did not know or understand about what the girl was talking.

questions.q: What was Peter’s response when he was asked a third time if he was one of Jesus’ disciples?
questions.a: Peter swore and put himself under curses that he did not know Jesus.

questions.q: What happened after Peter answered the third time?
questions.a: After Peter answered the third time, the rooster crowed a second time.

questions.q: What did Peter do after he heard the rooster?
questions.a: After he heard the rooster, Peter broke down and wept.

commentary.text: The passover, Jesus declares that Judas would betray him.

Verses 1–11 Did Christ pour out his soul unto death for us, and shall we think any thing too precious for him? Do we give him the precious ointment of our best affections? Let us love him with all the heart, though it is common for zeal and affection to be misunderstood and blamed; and remember that charity to the poor will not excuse any from particular acts of piety to the Lord Jesus. Christ commended this woman's pious attention to the notice of believers in all ages. Those who honour Christ he will honour. Covetousness was Judas' master lust, and that betrayed him to the sin of betraying his Master; the devil suited his temptation to that, and so conquered him. And see what wicked contrivances many have in their sinful pursuits; but what appears to forward their plans, will prove curses in the end.

Nothing could be less the result of human foresight than the events here related. But our Lord knows all things about us before they come to pass. If we admit him, he will dwell in our hearts. The Son of man goes, as it is written of him, as a lamb to the slaughter; but woe to that man by whom he is betrayed! God's permitting the sins of men, and bringing glory to himself out of them, does not oblige them to sin; nor will this be any excuse for their guilt, or lessen their punishment.

The Lord's supper is food for the soul, therefore a very little of that which is for the body, as much as will serve for a sign, is enough. It was instituted by the example and the practice of our Master, to remain in force till his second coming. It was instituted with blessing and giving of thanks, to be a memorial of Christ's death. Frequent mention is made of his precious blood, as the price of our redemption. How comfortable is this to poor repenting sinners, that the blood of Christ is shed for many! If for many, why not for me? It was a sign of the conveyance of the benefits purchased for us by his death. Apply the doctrine of Christ crucified to yourselves; let it be meat and drink to your souls, strengthening and refreshing your spiritual life. It was to be an earnest and foretaste of the happiness of heaven, and thereby to put us out of taste for the pleasures and delights of sense. Every one that has tasted spiritual delights, straightway desires eternal ones. Though the great Shepherd passed through his sufferings without one false step, yet his followers often have been scattered by the small measure of sufferings allotted to them. How very apt we are to think well of ourselves, and to trust our own hearts! It was ill done of Peter thus to answer his Master, and not with fear and trembling. Lord, give me grace to keep me from denying thee.

Christ's sufferings began with the sorest of all, those in his soul. He began to be sorely amazed; words not used in St. Matthew, but very full of meaning. The terrors of God set themselves in array against him, and he allowed him to contemplate them. Never was sorrow like unto his at this time. Now he was made a curse for us; the curses of the law were laid upon him as our Surety. He now tasted death, in all the bitterness of it. This was that fear of which the apostle speaks, the natural fear of pain and death, at which human nature startles. Can we ever entertain favourable, or even slight thoughts of sin, when we see the painful sufferings which sin, though but reckoned to him, brought on the Lord Jesus? Shall that sit light upon our souls, which sat so heavy upon his? Was Christ in such agony for our sins, and shall we never be in agony about them? How should we look upon Him whom we have pierced, and mourn! It becomes us to be exceedingly sorrowful for sin, because He was so, and never to mock at it. Christ, as Man, pleaded, that, if it were possible, his sufferings might pass from him. As Mediator, he submitted to the will of God, saying, Nevertheless, not what I will, but what thou wilt; I bid it welcome. See how the sinful weakness of Christ's disciples returns, and overpowers them. What heavy clogs these bodies of ours are to our souls! But when we see trouble at the door, we should get ready for it. Alas, even believers often look at the Redeemer's sufferings in a drowsy manner, and instead of being ready to die with Christ, they are not even prepared to watch with him one hour.

Because Christ appeared not as a temporal prince, but preached repentance, reformation, and a holy life, and directed men's thoughts, and affections, and aims to another world, therefore the Jewish rulers sought to destroy him. Peter wounded one of the band. It is easier to fight for Christ than to die for him. But there is a great difference between faulty disciples and hypocrites. The latter rashly and without thought call Christ Master, and express great affection for him, yet betray him to his enemies. Thus they hasten their own destruction.

We have here Christ's condemnation before the great council of the Jews. Peter followed; but the high priest's fire-side was no proper place, nor his servants proper company, for Peter: it was an entrance into temptation. Great diligence was used to procure false witnesses against Jesus, yet their testimony was not equal to the charge of a capital crime, by the utmost stretch of their law. He was asked, Art thou the Son of the Blessed? that is, the Son of God. For the proof of his being the Son of God, he refers to his second coming. In these outrages we have proofs of man's enmity to God, and of God's free and unspeakable love to man.

Peter's denying Christ began by keeping at a distance from him. Those that are shy of godliness, are far in the way to deny Christ. Those who think it dangerous to be in company with Christ's disciples, because thence they may be drawn in to suffer for him, will find it much more dangerous to be in company with his enemies, because there they may be drawn in to sin against him. When Christ was admired and flocked after, Peter readily owned him; but will own no relation to him now he is deserted and despised. Yet observe, Peter's repentance was very speedy. Let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall; and let him that has fallen think of these things, and of his own offences, and return to the Lord with weeping and supplication, seeking forgiveness, and to be raised up by the Holy Spirit.
